method: designlab.stage2.moves: Stage 1's transition (ZMP preview control on the designlab model) with its schedule passed as data; a commanded move (a stop, a turn) is causal

rules.S2A-causal: a commanded move (a stop, a turn) is causal: its reference is the periodic walk, frame for frame, up to the command frame; the preview controller first sees the commanded plan at that frame (the control law in its incremental form, so that new preview information enters only through its own increments); the move's file begins at the command frame, which is the command instant on a track. Before the command frame every array of the plan is the continuing walk's exactly; the CoM path there is the walk's up to the preview grid's step (the smallest frame interval of the whole commanded plan, so the grid, though nothing previewed, depends on the plan): two commanded plans from one walk agree before the command to under 0.05 mm of CoM, and exactly on one grid. A command may only be given at a lift-off (a multiple of half a stride). Named and not used: Stage 1's convention (decision 18: the command is the start of the reference's own ramp), under which the reference's CoM leaves the walk before the command; decision 18's reading is kept in every stop record (reference.stage1_stop). Starts and speed changes stay Stage 1's construction
rules.S2A-rule-F: committed footprints: a stance that began before the command keeps the footprint of the walk's own path (gait a's constant period, speed and yaw rate, from the same origin); a swing that lifts at or after the command lands on the commanded path
rules.S2A-fade: the causal transient (the cart-table ZMP of the preview controller's own output less its ZMP reference: what a controller without foreknowledge cannot track) is excused from the multibody-ZMP correction with the weight 1 - s((p - c - 0.5) / 0.5), s the minimum-jerk step: in full up to 0.5 stride after the command phase c, not at all from 1 stride after it; from there the loop corrects the multibody ZMP against the plan's target, as Stage 1's
rules.S2A-ramp: a turn's yaw rate and stride period ramp together over 0.375 s of reference time (minimum-jerk), for every set, body and rate: r = 2 x 0.375 / (T_walk + T_turn) strides
rules.S2A-appendage: inside a move whose stride period T(p) is shorter than the walk's, the tail's and the neck's swing amplitudes are multiplied by (T(p) / T_walk)^2 (constant angular acceleration amplitude), for every set, look sets included; a look choice (lead's ruling 1)
rules.S2A-stride: inside the turn the stride period is f x T_walk at the same path speed; f is the largest value of 1, 0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75, 0.7, 0.65, 0.6 for which the finite turn's own kinematic pass (the causal plan solved once, no ZMP correction), in both directions, has ik_ok, uses at most 0.85 of the usable thigh-twist range on the worse leg and leaves every other gated joint at least 0.05 rad of its usable range; the reference built with all passes must show ik_ok, at most 0.87 and the same 0.05 rad, else f steps down once (at most 2 times in all); constants set on the 14 Nov prototypes of V0 on 75-M-H-10, before any closed-loop run; the 0.05 rad is Stage 0's joint-range limit of a move (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A12 as amended: a start, change, stop or turn; every end of a joint's usable range but one it rests on by design; a walk keeps 0.1 rad), one constant with the set's screen; the rule read 0.1 rad from the morning of 15 Nov (A11's first amendment, withdrawn), under which V0's quick turn moved to f 0.7 and missed two gates and the two tuned sets had no factor (the owner's decision of 15 Nov, DECISION_LOG.md P34, after the first builds of the three sets; changed after a result)
rules.S2A-gates: a move passes when: ik_ok; its last output stride is within 1 mm of gait b's CoM and 2 mm of its multibody ZMP (the home stance for a stop); a move of Stage 1's construction: its first stride the same against gait a, and the final ZMP error at most 4 mm; a causal move: the warm-up stride and the command frame within 1 mm of the walk's CoM, joints within 0.001 rad at the command frame, multibody ZMP within 4 mm over the warm-up frames up to two frames before the command (the ZMP at the command frame is recorded, not gated: its central difference straddles the command), single-support CoP at least 10 mm inside the pad, consistency error over the first stride after the command at most 4.0 mm; ZMP error from one stride after it at most 4.0 mm (windows fixed on 15 Nov after the scratch builds of V0, before any set was frozen and before any closed-loop episode on a Stage 2 set: STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A7); a turn: total heading within 1e-09 rad of its angle, heading at the bar's instant at least 80 deg on the nominal commanded clock and on the slowest, thigh twist at most 0.87 of the usable range; the two-touchdown stop: exactly 2 touchdowns after the command, forward CoM speed below 5 % of the walk's within 1.5 strides of the command, 1 Hz low-passed forward CoM acceleration within 1.5 m/s^2 (a zero-phase order-2 Butterworth at 1 Hz turns a speed change dv into at most 2.22 x dv m/s^2, so this term detects rocking, not abruptness; the unfiltered peak is recorded beside it); constants set on the 14 Nov prototypes of V0 on 75-M-H-10, before any closed-loop run, but the ZMP readings of a causal move, which have one limit, Stage 1's 4 mm: the warm-up frames (it was 2 mm), the first stride after the command (it was 2.5 mm) and the frames after it (unchanged); the CoM's 1 mm and the joints' 0.001 rad at the command stand as written (the owner's decision of 15 Nov, DECISION_LOG.md P34, after the first builds of the three sets; changed after a result)
rules.S2S-process: every array is made inside s2io.r2() (gait accuracy r2, checked on entry and on exit) with one BLAS thread, each item in a fresh process on a body rebuilt for it (look.source); a walk's inverse dynamics, summary and both array formats come from the one generation in the one block
rules.S2S-twins: where Stage 1's run (stage1/runs/2026-11-08/<body>) holds a walk of the same spec, or a transition between walks of the same specs made with Stage 1's own schedule, the set's file must have its sha256; where the look ladder (stage2/look/look_refs.json) holds a rung of the same spec, the look-format file must have its sha256; a difference stops the build with both hashes (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A4).  V0 owes them: on a body that has a Stage 1 run record its nominal and start must be Stage 1's own files, and on a body the look ladder holds its look-format nominal and v0.4 must be the ladder's rungs; a twin that is not found there stops the build and fails sets verify (SetDef.stage1_twins, ladder_twins)
rules.S2S-stage0: the Stage 0 gates that block a freeze (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A12) are read where a reference is built, with the set screen's own functions: a walk by setscreen.judge_walk on its look.price, a move by setscreen.screen_move on its file; the set's screen.json is made afterwards by setscreen and must agree (sets verify)
rules.S2S-fallback: a start, change or stop that fails a gate of its entry (A7) or a blocking Stage 0 gate (A12) is retried in this order and no other (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A8): (1) a change with a ramp of 2 strides instead of 1 (same name; the entry records ramp_strides 2 and this rule); (2) for a ladder rung other than 0.40 m/s, a change from the neighbouring rung toward 0.40 m/s (v0.4_to_v0.45, v0.45_to_v0.5, v0.4_to_v0.35, v0.35_to_v0.3), with one stride of ramp, the rung's plan then walking through 0.40 m/s; (3) the item is recorded 'no transition within the gates' with its numbers.  A start and the stops have no fallback and nominal_to_v0.4 has step (1) only.  A failed start or nominal_to_v0.4 stops the set and goes to the lead (a set that starts into its 0.40 m/s walk, S2S-lead-in: a failed start_v0.4)
rules.S2S-lead-in: a set whose nominal walk is a rung starts into it (start; set.json lead_in 'start').  A set whose nominal walk is not a rung (A12) but whose 0.40 m/s walk is starts from standing straight into its 0.40 m/s walk: start_v0.4, built and gated like start, with no fallback; set.json says lead_in 'start_v0.4', and so does every record of the set (an exception, labelled where its rows are printed).  The items that need the nominal walk are then not available, with that reason, and a ladder rung is reached by the fallback rule's step (2), a change from the neighbouring rung toward 0.40 m/s.  A start_v0.4 that fails a gate stops the set: it is not run.  A set with neither walk has no lead-in (lead_in null) and its conditions are not run (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A8 as amended: the owner's decision of 15 Nov, DECISION_LOG.md P34, after the first builds of the three sets; changed after a result)
rules.S2S-turns: a turn rate is built once for both directions (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A10, A11): moves.pick_stride_factor on the set's 0.40 m/s walk, both directions with all passes at the chosen factor, then moves.step_down on the built pair (ik_ok in both, the worse thigh-twist use, the tighter margin of another joint, a leg drive over a Stage 0 limit in either, a neck or tail limit in either).  No factor, or a leg drive over its limit: 'no reference within the thigh twist and the leg drives', and the reason also names the entry gates the last built pair missed.  A built turn that fails another gate (A7's, A10's heading readings, another blocking gate of A12) has no further retry and no reference; where only the heading readings fail: 'no reference within the heading rule'.  A turn over a neck or tail limit alone is kept with a1_over true
rules.S2S-not-available: an item with no reference is an entry with available false, a reason and its numbers, and no file; it is listed in set.json not_available; a walk that fails a blocking Stage 0 gate is dropped from the ladder in this way and no move is built from or to it (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A8, A11, A12).  No ramp, grid, gate or constant is changed for it.  Its verdict is the code's that built it (built_by): while the set is not frozen, a build by other Stage 2 modules makes it again; an array an earlier build left under its name is removed
